categories.name: AI-Powered Vulnerability Research
categories.summary: Major developments in AI-assisted vulnerability discovery dominated today's feed. Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview has uncovered over 10,000 high/critical vulnerabilities through Project Glasswing, prompting calls for shorter patch cycles. New open-source frameworks like OpenHack are packaging agent-driven vuln research into accessible coding harnesses, signaling maturation of AI security tooling.

key_items.title: Claude Mythos discovers 10K+ critical vulnerabilities in one month
key_items.detail: Anthropic's unreleased frontier model has surfaced massive vulnerability counts in essential software, pushing the company to advise developers to accelerate patching cadence.

key_items.title: OpenHack: Open-source AI vulnerability research workspace
key_items.detail: New file-based workspace enables agent-driven vuln research in coding harnesses like Claude Code and Cursor; emphasizes treating inputs and toolchains as supply-chain trust boundaries.

key_items.title: CERT.PL on autonomous fuzzing
key_items.detail: Technical post exploring autonomous fuzzing methodologies for vulnerability discovery.

categories.name: AI Agent Security & Controls
categories.summary: As AI agents move from demos to production toolchains, security boundaries around agent harnesses are becoming critical. Multiple posts emphasized the need for explicit controls on repo scope, tool execution, and disclosure workflows—especially as frontier models like Mythos may soon integrate into coding environments.

key_items.title: Claude Mythos may integrate into Claude Code
key_items.detail: BleepingComputer reports signals of Mythos model surfacing in Claude Code; teams will need controls for scope, execution, triage, and disclosure if frontier vuln-discovery models enter coding agents.

key_items.title: Pentest Agent Suite for autonomous bug bounty
key_items.detail: Framework brings autonomous bug-bounty capabilities to Claude Code and AI coding tools; security boundary is the harness controlling scope files, MCP servers, and exploit steps.

categories.name: LLM Security & Prompt Injection
categories.summary: Detection gaps in AI security stacks continue to be a concern. Today's coverage highlighted prompt injection patterns that bypass traditional WAF/EDR because payloads arrive as trusted context through RAG retrieval and agent tool calls, requiring logging of retrieval slices and tool I/O before privileged actions.

key_items.title: Three prompt injection patterns evading detection stacks
key_items.detail: Patterns bypass WAF/EDR by embedding payloads in trusted context; mitigation requires logging RAG slices, tool-call I/O, and conversation changes before model actions.

categories.name: Security Tools & Releases
categories.summary: A notable LLM red-teaming toolkit was released today. Cryptex OSS provides 162 transforms, 36 mutators, and 25 tool surfaces for testing prompt and agent defenses, enabling repeatable security evaluations across mutation variants.

key_items.title: Cryptex OSS: LLM red-team toolkit released
key_items.detail: MIT-licensed toolkit with extensive transforms and mutators for testing AI defenses; recommends isolated runs with logged payloads for reproducibility.

top_insights: Frontier AI models are accelerating vulnerability discovery at unprecedented scale, with Claude Mythos finding 10K+ critical bugs in one month—fundamentally changing the attacker-defender timeline.
The integration of vulnerability-discovery models into coding agents represents a significant shift requiring new security control paradigms around scope, execution, and disclosure.
Traditional security detection (WAF/EDR) is increasingly blind to AI-specific attack vectors where malicious payloads arrive as trusted context through RAG and tool calls.
Open-source AI security tooling is maturing rapidly, with both offensive (Cryptex OSS red-teaming) and defensive (OpenHack research workspaces) capabilities becoming accessible.
Supply-chain trust boundaries around AI agent harnesses are emerging as a critical security consideration as autonomous security tools move into production.
